svg.title: How the system works out a price
svg.text: Each Procedure on a Booking is priced on its own
One Contract per priced item, picked by the office
at booking setup and changeable by the
anaesthetist until the List is authorised. Its own
settings give its pricing kind and who it bills.
No contract · RVG is always offered first.
Sets the base units. Required on an RVG price; on a
fixed or open price it is for reference only. The
Contract's default RVG code may fill it in.
RVG price only. From start and finish: 1 per 15 min
for the first 2 h, then 1 per 10 min, part interval
RVG price only. Picked one by one by the
anaesthetist, each with a short note, because
Each anaesthetist sets their own dollar value per
unit, used on an RVG price at their rate or less a
discount. Never a shared price list.
The List's date. On a fixed price it picks the price
range in force on that day.
The Procedure holds its units and any typed price;
rate and discount come from the pricing kind.
Not held on the Procedure, never edited here
No reason needed · audited and flagged at review ·
the last change stands. The anaesthetist may also
type the amount on No contract · Fixed price.
St George's does not allow the override: the
A price nobody typed is worked out, not stored: a new
price range, or a rate or discount edited on the
Contract, reaches every Procedure on it not yet
authorised, unless its prepayment invoice holds it.
Changing the Contract clears a typed price; the
recorded RVG detail is kept. Only the office moves
a Procedure onto or off a prepaid Contract.
First match wins: a price the Procedure holds,
Frozen in the snapshot at AUTHORISED; the prepaid
amount once its prepayment invoice is raised; or a
BTM: base, time and modifier units. A discount is
a fraction (10% is 0.1), shown as its own invoice line.
A price of $0 gives a no-charge invoice.
An open price with no amount, or a fixed price
with no range in force on the date. It stops the
anaesthetist completing (they can send it on to
the office) and stops the List being authorised.
More than one Procedure on a Booking
Base units go on the primary Procedure only.
Time units go on every Procedure, from its own
times. Modifier units go on the primary when
four or fewer; above four they are spread as
evenly as possible, the remainder to the primary
carry units, and no Contract changes this.
Each Contract bills its holder or the payer on
the Booking; that sets the invoice destination.
Bills the payer: No contract · RVG, prepay price
lists, surgeons' fixed fees such as Merivale.
Bills the List's hospital, with a funding tag
Bills any other holder: an insurer or funder,
a surgeon group, an untagged hospital.
Payer: the person named on the Booking
Prefilled from the patient; can be changed to a
parent, guardian or another party who pays.
One invoice per billable party per Booking.
Snapshot when the List is authorised
The Contract's settings as they then were
Recorded BTM units and the rate used
Contracts are edited in place, so it copies them.
Later changes to the RVG or a Contract never
change an invoice that has been issued.
One H3 anaesthetic on 21 Jul 2026: 6 base + 7 time + 1 modifier = 14 units, anaesthetist's own value $40
RVG at the anaesthetist's rate, 14 units
RVG less a discount, 10% set on the Contract
RVG at the Contract's rate, $42 a unit
Fixed price, range from 1 Jun 2026: $3,100; RVG code for reference
Range from 1 Jul 2026 added later: $3,200, before authorising
Dr B. Smith · Face lift, prepaid
Fixed price $1,200, held by the prepayment invoice
Prepaid · Fixed price, via Other price
Open price: $2,000 typed by the office
Any typed price cleared, RVG detail kept, 14 units
Price overridden to $0 by the anaesthetist
Flow: Contract and RVG detail → a held price, else the pricing kind → holder or payer billed → snapshot·Still open: mixed-Booking base units (OQ-132), modifiers (OQ-95)
